page: The Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g-3840s is a high-capacity instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family, designed for resource-heavy workloads requiring balanced compute and memory along with high-speed local disk capacity. The instance provides 64 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory provisioning stands at 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Fast local storage is directly integrated into the instance, featuring a 3840 GB NVMe SSD array, while graphical processing units are absent.

Hardware benchmark testing shows competitive performance across both single-threaded and parallel processing operations. The AMD EPYC processor features modern vector extensions, including AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16, facilitating strong results in CPU-intensive tasks such as PassMark CPU execution, Clang compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks, where it ranks in the top tier. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 496.98 GB/sec and write bandwidth hits 190.5 GB/sec, matching its top-tier throughput capabilities. In-memory data structures also execute efficiently, evidenced by Redis processing exceeding 104 million SET operations per second and high scores in database transaction testing.

With its combination of dedicated physical cores, high memory bandwidth, and 3840 GB of bundled NVMe storage, the server eliminates external disk latency and network storage bottlenecks. Because the hardware maintains a standard compute-to-memory balance alongside substantial direct-attached solid-state capacity, it delivers high operational efficiency for disk-bound and transactional services without incurring standalone networked volume overhead.

The vx1-g-64c-256g-3840s is primarily suited for large relational databases, distributed datastores, static web serving clusters, large-scale CI/CD software compilation pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference pipelines executing on medium and small models.
description: The Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g-3840s is a general-purpose, storage-rich compute instance powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor. The configuration delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores clocked at 2.0 GHz, 256 GB of system memory, and 3840 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. It excludes discrete GPU hardware. Hardware benchmarks highlight top-tier performance in single-core and multi-core evaluations, including high scores in compilation, ray tracing, and database operations, complemented by large-block uncached memory read bandwidth of nearly 497 GB/sec. The instance delivers steady execution throughput across parallel threads, supported by AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets. This resource balance makes the server well suited for production database servers, heavy CI/CD build environments, large Redis caching tiers, and medium-scale CPU inference workloads requiring substantial low-latency storage capacity.
